questions.q: Find the simple interest on ₹8000 at 5% per annum for 3 years.
questions.e: SI = P × R × T / 100 = 8000 × 5 × 3 / 100 = ₹1200. ₹400 is only one year, and ₹1261 would be the compound interest.

questions.q: At what rate per annum will ₹1500 earn a simple interest of ₹270 in 3 years?
questions.e: R = SI × 100 / (P × T) = 270 × 100 / (1500 × 3) = 6%. Forgetting to divide by the 3 years gives 18%.

questions.q: In how many years will ₹2000 earn a simple interest of ₹480 at 8% per annum?
A sum earns a simple interest of ₹360 in 2 years at 6% per annum. Find the sum.
questions.e: P = SI × 100 / (R × T) = 360 × 100 / (6 × 2) = ₹3000. Using only R in the denominator gives ₹6000.

questions.q: What amount will ₹5000 become in 2½ years at 4% simple interest per annum?
questions.e: SI = 5000 × 4 × 2.5 / 100 = ₹500, so the amount is 5000 + 500 = ₹5500. ₹500 alone is the interest.

questions.q: Find the compound interest on ₹10000 for 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually.
questions.e: Amount = 10000 × 1.1 × 1.1 = 12100, so CI = ₹2100. ₹2000 is the simple interest.

questions.q: What is the amount on ₹4000 for 2 years at 5% per annum compound interest?
questions.e: Amount = 4000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = ₹4410. ₹4400 is the simple-interest amount.

questions.q: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. The rate of interest per annum is
questions.e: Interest equals the principal in 8 years, so 8 × R = 100 and R = 12.5%.

questions.q: Find the compound interest on ₹8000 for 1 year at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly.
questions.e: Rate is 5% per half-year for 2 half-years: 8000 × 1.05² = 8820, so CI = ₹820. ₹800 is the annual figure.

₹5000 is invested at simple interest, with the rate 4% in the first year, 5% in the second year and 6% in the third year. The interest earned in 3 years is
questions.e: Interest = 5000 × (4 + 5 + 6) / 100 = ₹750. Taking 4% or 6% for all 3 years gives ₹600 or ₹900.

questions.q: What is the compound interest on ₹8000 for 3 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually?
questions.e: Amount = 8000 × 1.1³ = 10648, so CI = 10648 − 8000 = ₹2648. ₹2400 is the simple interest.

questions.q: Find the compound interest on ₹16000 for 1½ years at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly.
questions.e: Rate 5% per half-year for 3 periods: 16000 × 1.05³ = 18522, so CI = ₹2522. ₹2400 is the simple interest.

questions.q: On ₹5000 at 8% per annum for 2 years, how much more is the compound interest than the simple interest?

questions.e: After year 1 the amount is ₹5500, and 10% of it is ₹550. ₹500 is the first-year interest.

What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹10000 for 3 years at 10% per annum?
questions.e: CI = 10000 × (1.331 − 1) = ₹3310 and SI = ₹3000, so the difference is ₹310. ₹331 is the CI per 1000.

questions.q: For a certain sum, the simple interest for 2 years is ₹600 and the compound interest for 2 years is ₹630. The sum is
questions.e: CI − SI = 30 is the interest on the first year's SI of 300, so R = 30/300 × 100 = 10%. Then P = 600 × 100 / (10 × 2) = ₹3000.

questions.q: ₹8000 is invested for 1 year at 20% per annum. How much more interest is earned if it is compounded half-yearly than if it is compounded annually?
questions.e: Half-yearly: 8000 × 1.1² = 9680, interest ₹1680. Annually: interest ₹1600. The difference is ₹80.
